title: model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Title: Model Regression Forensics Playbook

Overview:
This playbook codifies the steps, checks, and commands for investigating model quality regressions surfaced by our eval harness, prompt-sets, or customer reports. Its scope covers regressions introduced by model artifacts, quantization changes, runtime/kernel upgrades, prompt template drift, and eval harness configuration changes. Target audience: ML engineers, serving runtime owners, SRE, and product owners.

Quick summary of when to use this playbook:
- Automated alerts from eval-harness show >= 3 percentage point drop on core prompt set in last deploy window.
- Customer-reported quality degradation with reproducible examples.
- Regression detected in nightly benchmark: median BLEU/ROUGE/accuracy drop exceeding configured thresholds.

Severity thresholds (when to open an incident):
1. Sev-1: Production SLA-affecting and customer-facing regression where pass rate drop >= 10 percentage points or catastrophic hallucination surge observed across 5%+ traffic.
2. Sev-2: Noticeable degradation (3-10 percentage points) on core prompts or failure in critical QA pipelines.
3. Sev-3: Minor drift or single-model variant issue reported by internal evals.

Operational SLOs and monitoring queries (examples):
- Quality SLO: core_prompt_set_pass_rate >= 95%.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for text-generation endpoints.
- Regression alert (prometheus-style):
  - expression: increase(rate(eval_harness_failed_prompts[6h])) > 0.03
  - trigger: sustained for 30 minutes

Prioritized hypothesis checklist (run in order):
1. Deployment / artifact change
   - New model artifact (model-vX) pushed, or weights replaced.
   - Model packaging changed (tokenizer version, special tokens).
2. Quantization/profile mismatch
   - New quant profile applied (int8/fp16 vs previous fp16).
   - Quant kernel mismatch for specific GPUs.
3. Runtime/kernel or driver change
   - CUDA/cuDNN/Rocm upgrades or patched inference kernels.
4. Inference config change
   - Beam/search/temperature/stop-sequences changed globally or per-route.
5. Prompt or template drift
   - Prompt set was updated (typo, template placeholder change).
6. Eval-harness/config change
   - New sampling seed, batch size, or normalization in scoring.
7. Upstream data / tokenization changes
   - Tokenizer vocab update or special character handling changed.

Forensic checklist (commands and queries):
1) Reproduce locally with eval harness (deterministic run)
   - Command: python -m eval_harness.run
       --model-path /redwood/models/model-vX
       --prompt-file prompts/core_prompt_set.jsonl
       --seed 42
       --num-samples 1000
       --output results/regression-local.json
   - Compare aggregated metrics: python -m eval_harness.compare --baseline baseline-2026-02-20.json results/regression-local.json

2) Run against hosted endpoint (production config)
   - curl example:
     curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
       -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY'
       -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
       -d '{"model":"model-vX","prompt":"{{prompt}}","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":128}' | jq '.choices[0].text'
   - Ensure temperature=0 and deterministic sampling when reproducing for forensics.

3) Compare tokenization/ids for failing prompts
   - python -c "from tokenizer import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.load('model-vX'); print(t.encode('Example → text'))"
   - If token sequence differs from baseline, flag tokenizer mismatch.

4) Evaluate quantization-specific differences
   - Run small-batch float32 vs quantized inference on same hardware:
     python -m perf.run_infer --model model-vX --quant none --input sample_inputs.jsonl --output results/fp32.json
     python -m perf.run_infer --model model-vX --quant int8 --input sample_inputs.jsonl --output results/int8.json
   - Diff outputs token-by-token: python -m eval_harness.token_diff results/fp32.json results/int8.json

5) Kernel/runtime checks
   - Check GPU driver and kernel versions on nodes that served the traffic:
     ssh gpu-node-01 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name --format=csv'
   - Compare with last-known-good driver pinned in infra docs.

6) Batching/throughput effects
   - Temporarily force single-request inference to isolate batching side effects:
     curl -X POST https://host/route?batching=0 ...
   - If regression disappears, suspect KV-cache or batch-reordering bug.

7) Eval harness config diff
   - git diff -- prompts/core_prompt_set.jsonl eval-harness/config.yaml
   - Check seeds, normalization, scoring function, and pass/fail thresholds.

Metric forensic queries (examples):
- SQL: Find prompts with the largest delta in pass rate since last deploy
  SELECT prompt_id, baseline_pass_rate, current_pass_rate, current_pass_rate - baseline_pass_rate AS delta
  FROM eval_results
  WHERE run_date >= '2026-02-01' AND model_version IN ('model-vX', 'model-vX-quant')
  ORDER BY delta ASC LIMIT 25;

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- Triage lead (first 30m): oncall-ml (engineering)
- Model artifact owner: persona/model-owner (engineering)
- Serving runtime owner: infra-serving (engineering)
- Quantization specialist: applied-ml (engineering)
- SRE: eng-sre (for capacity/driver/runtime issues)
- Product lead: product (product)

Decision and mitigation steps (ordered):
1. Short-term mitigation (first hour):
   - If regression is service- or model-specific, route traffic to previous model variant (rollback):
     - API: POST /admin/route with body {"route":"/v1/generate","model":"model-vW"}
   - If quantization suspected, revert to fp16 build for affected pool.
2. Medium-term (2-24 hours):
   - Deploy targeted canary with FP32 or previous quant profile for 5% traffic and monitor eval-harness pass rate.
   - Run full eval-harness on staging with identical runtime and batching.
3. Long-term (48-72 hours):
   - Root cause analysis, postmortem, update quantization profiles or packaging, add regression tests to the eval-harness pipeline.

Rollback matrix (example):
| Situation | Immediate action | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| New model artifact causing regression | Route to previous stable model | oncall-ml/model-owner | Maintain audit of traffic shift |
| Quantized build degraded | Rebuild and route to fp16 | applied-ml/infra-serving | Add additional quantization regression tests |
| Kernel/driver bug | Roll GPUs to previous driver/disable node pool | eng-sre | Notify infra procurement if hardware upgrade required |

Postmortem template (minimum content):
- Summary: brief description + impact window
- Timeline: deploys, alerts, customer reports, mitigations
- Root cause(s): one or more items from hypothesis checklist with evidence
- Corrective actions: short/medium/long-term (owners and due dates)
- Test and automation changes: new evals, CI gates, canary configs

Prevention: CI and eval-harness gates to add/modify
- Block merges that change model packaging without an explicit packaging spec PR and regression-test run.
- Add a nightly cross-profile regression run: for each model, run FP32, FP16, and int8 profiles and compare core prompt set.
- Add a quant-profiles smoke test in the release pipeline that checks token-level fidelity on 200 golden prompts.

Appendix: useful scripts and references
- Eval harness run: /scripts/eval/run_local.sh
- Token diff tool: /tools/token_diff.py --help
- Canaries: /infra/traffic-shifting/README.md
- Quantization profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/index

Contacts (oncall rotation):
- oncall-ml: ml-oncall@redwood.ai
- eng-sre: sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- applied-ml: applied-ml@redwood.ai

Notes and caveats:
- Deterministic reproduction requires temperature=0 and fixed seed for sampling-aware models. For beam/greedy, ensure beam size and length-penalty match.
- Some regressions are dataset-dependent and will not appear on the core prompt set; maintain an augmented customer-reported prompt set for higher coverage.
- When rolling back, preserve detailed request traces and eval artifacts for later analysis.

Last reviewed: 2026-02-25 by reviewers listed above.
